newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee hits 7-mth high vs dlr, RBI keeps off.
newsitem.headline: India rupee hits 7-mth high vs dlr, RBI keeps off.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) kept off the market even as the rupee touched a seven-month high of 35.735 per dollar on Thursday on poor demand for the U.S. currency, dealers said.
"They (RBI) made some enquiries but did not come to the market to buy dollars," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"This (RBI's inaction) combined with the poor dollar demand pushed the rupee up although supply was pretty normal," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said the rupee traded at a high of 35.735 and a low of 35.765 on Thursday.
"Trade was quite thin, with the market consisting mainly of sellers," said a dealer. "The rupee last touched 35.73 on December 4 and 35.74 on April 24."
Dealers said the rupee appreciated above 35.75 as some banks unwound long dollar positions.
"A number of banks were sitting on long dollar positions looking for the RBI to come in and buy dollars," said a dealer at a public sector bank.
"As the rupee kept rising through the day and the RBI stayed away, they were forced to unwind their positions. This pushed the rupee up," he said.
Dealers said the outlook for Friday was uncertain.
"It is a bit confusing," said a dealer. "Based on its past actions, everyone expected the RBI to step in once the rupee hit 35.75 but now it is not clear what their intentions are."
"We will have to wait and see."

Some dealers said the RBI was constrained in its forex market intervention by the impact this has on the domestic money market. RBI dollar purchases inject rupees into the banking system and boost money supply growth.
The latest RBI data shows year-on-year growth in M3 money supply at 16.6 percent for teh fortnight ended June 6. It has set a target of 15.0-15.5 percent for 1997/98 (April-MArch).
"Maybe RBI is worried about M3 growth and has decided not to intervene," said a dealer.
Other dealers said they expected RBI to buy dollars aggressively on Friday and stem the rupee's rise.
"RBI cannot sit back and watch the rupee rise for long," said another dealer. "There should be some action tomorrow and the rupee will drop back below 35.75."
Dealers said the rupee was largely steady in the forward market and rose slightly on dollar demand from importers.
"We saw some demand for June-delivery dollars," said a dealer. "Thre was some demand but supply was more than enough to meet deamnd. Trade was basically quiet with a slight rise in forward premiums."
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Thursday at 3.64 percent against Wednesday's 3.41 percent, dealers said.
